agentCan: Implement the per-customer-org authorize/token flow and refresh handling
Author the FDK app configuration if you take the Marketplace flavor (the platform then manages the handshake and token storage)

approval.cost: No listing fee, review fee, or revenue-share figure is stated in the docs read (global apps 'can be published as Freshworks paid apps on the Freshworks Marketplace for all products except Freshsales Classic')
approval.trigger: OAuth credentials themselves: no review (self-serve Settings action). Custom apps: explicitly NOT reviewed ('A custom app is not subject to review; it is available for installation as soon as it is submitted and published'; distribution by manual upload of the packaged FDK artifact, private to one product account). Freshworks Marketplace apps and External apps: review is required before publication/listing. Clicking 'Save and Publish' submits 'the app for the approval process'; the app shows as Draft Version (Under Review), and 'After the app is reviewed and approved, it is published to the Freshworks Marketplace' (for External apps it is listed in the Marketplace while installation happens from the third-party's URL). Review is tracked across five categories: Code ('Code quality, security, and platform compliance'), QA ('Functional testing'), Content ('Listing content, links, category, screenshots, video, and descriptions'), Security ('Security and privacy review'), Business ('Business and marketplace policy review'); statuses run Draft/In Development, Under Review, Changes requested / Ready to publish / Rejected, Published. No numeric user/install cap before approval is stated; 'selective access' via a hidden listing plus an account-specific shareable URL is documented only after publication.
approval.wait: Not stated (no review duration in the official docs read)

blockers.detail: After the 365-day refresh-token lifetime, 'the access token is not updated and all REST API calls fail with a 401 - Unauthorized error'. There is no silent renewal: an admin (account-level, via App Gallery > Settings > Reauthorize) or agent (agent-level, via a REAUTHORIZE button) must reauthorize, and your app 'should guide the app users to do this' with clear error messaging.
blockers.howToClear: Calendar the 365-day cliff per connection, monitor for 401s, and build the reauthorize path before you need it.
blockers.title: 365-day reauthorization cliff

blockers.detail: 'While you can add new scopes, removing scopes that are already selected is not supported' when updating OAuth credentials. And 'the mapping between OAuth apps and OAuth credentials is 1-1. A configured OAuth credential can only be used with one app': uploading another app with the same credentials errors in the App Management Portal.
blockers.howToClear: Choose scopes conservatively at creation (you can add later, never remove) and create separate credentials per app.
blockers.title: Scopes are additive-only; credentials are 1:1 with apps

blockers.detail: Authorize/token URLs embed the Freshworks organization domain, which differs per customer; hardcoding yours breaks other customers and breaks on domain change/transfer. Capture the domain at install (oauth_iparams).
blockers.howToClear: Build per-customer domain handling into the connect flow from day one.
blockers.title: Per-customer org domains

tested: Read-only verification: credential creation, the External-app journey, token lifetimes, scope and mapping rules, and the app-type review matrix were checked against current developers.freshworks.com documentation (no credentials created, nothing submitted). Source note from the research: Freshworks' App SDK docs are templated across products (Freshdesk = support_* modules; the pages read were service_* variants carrying identical platform text with Freshdesk examples).
unverified: Review timeline for Freshworks/External Marketplace apps (statuses and categories are documented; no duration).
Any listing/review cost or revenue share for Marketplace or paid apps.

Exact Freshdesk-specific scope strings (the credentials UI lists per-product resource permissions; the docs' worked examples use Freshservice/Freshchat scope names, and a Freshdesk scope catalog was not in the pages read).

Whether the External (non-FDK) token endpoint accepts the same Basic-header client authentication in all cases (documented explicitly in the oauth_config.json format; the External-app journey page states only that 'your app logic' places the access-token request).
Standalone REST API rate limits for OAuth tokens (not covered in the pages read).

alternatives: FDK Freshworks (Marketplace) app: 'OAuth handshake is completely taken care by the Freshworks Developer Platform' (it constructs the authorization-code and access-token requests from config/oauth_config.json and stores the tokens); token_type 'account' (handshake when an admin installs) or 'agent' (when an agent installs; cannot be 'agent' for serverless/background apps, and only one OAuth configuration per app may be agent-type)
Custom app (an FDK app private to a single customer account; no review)

Freshdesk API key as a secure installation parameter (iparams), used as Basic auth (per-account credential collection, not delegated OAuth; documented in Freshworks' own tutorial but not recommended for multi-tenant SaaS)
flavor.recommended: An External OAuth app using Freshworks OAuth credentials, running the authorization-code flow against each customer's Freshworks organization domain
flavor.why: External apps are 'non-Freshworks apps, built using third-party SDKs (or other provisions)': your app routes the user to the Freshworks authorization server at https://<org_url>/oauth/v2/authorize, the user picks an account, reviews the consent form, and clicks Agree, and your app exchanges the returned code at the org token endpoint. The OAuth object is a set of OAuth credentials (one client_id / client_secret pair) created in the Developer Portal under Settings > OAuth Credentials, bound 1:1 to one app. Note: 'To submit a Freshworks or External app, you only need a Freshworks Developer account. An active product subscription is not required.' (Custom apps are the exception.)

humanMust: Create/sign in to a Freshworks Developer account and open your organization
Create the OAuth credentials in the Developer Portal and record the Client ID and Client Secret
The customer's admin/agent reviews the consent form and clicks Agree at connect time
For Marketplace/External listing: submit via Developer Portal > Public App > Create New App and complete the App Information, Media and Installation, Support Details, and Privacy and Security tabs
name: Freshdesk
nuances: Access tokens live 30 minutes; in the platform-managed FDK flow 'the developer platform places a refresh-access-token call to the authorization server and regenerates the access token'. Refresh tokens live 365 days.

'When a user is deleted from an organization or removed from an account, the authorization server revokes any consents given to OAuth apps in that account and delete the refresh tokens issued to those apps. So, any subsequent API requests will fail.'

Multi-OAuth and multi-account ceilings (FDK platform): v3.0 allows a maximum of three OAuth-secured resources per app; v3.1+ allows five, with only one configuration facilitating agent installation; multi-account access supports 'up to 20 accounts per OAuth-secured resource' (account-level only). Agent-level OAuth 'cannot be used from the server.js file'. Up to five redirect URLs per credential set.

Marketplace code-coverage gate (FDK apps): 'For Marketplace submission, fdk pack requires a minimum of 50% coverage for statements, branches, functions, and lines'; if unit tests are configured, fdk pack requires at least 80% coverage per metric.

Module lock-in after publishing (FDK global apps): 'in the subsequent versions of the app, you cannot remove modules (that is, downgrade the number of modules)'. The credential name (max 3 words) and description are exactly what users see in the authorization window; the docs recommend matching the app-submission name.
prerequisites: A Freshworks Developer account (no active product subscription required for Freshworks/External apps)
Credential name (max 3 words) and description (both shown in the authorization window), redirect URL(s) (max five), and scope selections
Per-customer org-domain handling in your connect flow

steps.detail: 'To submit a Freshworks or External app, you only need a Freshworks Developer account. An active product subscription is not required.' Sign in and open your organization.
steps.title: Create a Freshworks Developer account

steps.detail: Developer login > enter organization/account URL > Settings (gear) > OAuth Credentials > Create OAuth Credentials: name (max 3 words, shown in the authorization window), description (also shown), redirect URL(s) (maximum five), and scopes in the Add scopes section. Click Create Credentials and record the Client ID and Client Secret.
steps.title: Create the OAuth credentials

steps.detail: For each customer, build the authorize URL on THAT customer's org domain (never hardcode): response_type=code, client_id, state (mandatory, randomly generated), scope (space-separated; 'You may include all or a subset of the scopes as selected in the OAuth credentials. Ensure that you do not include scopes that are not selected in your OAuth credentials'), redirect_uri (must be one registered on the credentials). The user picks an account, reviews the consent form (which separates scopes already approved from scopes awaiting approval), and clicks Agree; cancelling leaves 'the OAuth app remains unauthorized and non-functional'.
steps.title: Implement the per-customer connect flow

steps.detail: Exchange the code at the org token endpoint and store the access token and refresh token per customer org; call the Freshdesk REST APIs with the access token as a bearer token. Access tokens live 30 minutes; refresh tokens 365 days.
steps.title: Exchange the code; store tokens per org

steps.detail: Implement refresh before expiry and guide users through reauthorization when refresh fails (account-level: App Gallery > app > Settings > Reauthorize; agent-level FDK apps: a REAUTHORIZE button via client.interface.trigger('reAuthorize')).
steps.title: Handle refresh and reauthorization

steps.detail: Custom app: no review, installable as soon as submitted and published. Marketplace/External: Developer Portal > Public App > Create New App, complete App Information, Media and Installation, Support Details, and Privacy and Security tabs, then Save and Publish to submit for the five-category approval (Code, QA, Content, Security, Business).
steps.title: Distribute (Custom, or Marketplace/External with review)

tagline: The same Freshworks platform OAuth as Freshsales, aimed at support: credentials are self-service and Custom apps skip review, but Marketplace and External listings face the five-category Freshworks review with no stated turnaround, and every connection carries the platform's 365-day refresh-token expiry.

time.active: ~15 min of credential setup + ~1-2 hrs of per-org flow code
time.total: Same day for Custom apps and unlisted External use; Marketplace publication waits on a review with no stated duration
